title: Adverbs of Manner: quickly, well, hard
grammarTitle: Adverbs of Manner — How do you do it?
grammarNote: Наречия образа действия (adverbs of manner) описывают КАК выполняется действие. По-русски они отвечают на вопрос "Как?" — быстро, хорошо, медленно, тяжело. В английском большинство образуется добавлением -ly к прилагательному: quick → quickly. Но есть важные ИСКЛЮЧЕНИЯ, которые нужно запомнить: good → well, hard → hard, fast → fast.

grammarTable.subject: Adjective
grammarTable.example: quick → quickly · slow → slowly · careful → carefully

grammarTable.subject: Ending -le
grammarTable.example: simple → simply · comfortable → comfortably · gentle → gently

grammarTable.subject: Ending -y
grammarTable.example: easy → easily · heavy → heavily · happy → happily

grammarTable.subject: early
grammarTable.example: "He arrives early every day." — "earlily" does NOT exist!

grammarExtra.title: Position — WHERE does the adverb of manner go?

rows.example: She speaks clearly. · He runs quickly. · Amir studies hard.

rows.form: After the object (if there is one)
rows.example: She reads the text carefully. · He explained the problem clearly.
✗ "She reads carefully the text." → ✅ "She reads the text carefully."
"She is remarkably organised." · "He works incredibly hard."

grammarExtra.title: good vs well — the most common mistake

rows.example: She is a good student. · He has a good routine. · It was a good idea.
She studies well. · He organises his time well. · It works well.
"Are you well?" = "Are you healthy?" — not the same as good!
✅ "She speaks English well." — describes the verb "speaks".

grammarExtra.title: hard vs hardly — a false friend!

rows.example: "He works hard." = He puts in a lot of effort. Positive meaning.
"He hardly works." = He barely does any work. Very different meaning!
"It's a hard exam." — adjective modifying noun.
"She hardly ever skips class." ≈ "She almost never skips class."
He drives fast. She works hard. They arrive early.

grammarTip:
Три вещи, которые нельзя забыть:
① good → well. Запомни навсегда: "I speak English WELL" (не "good"). Это самая частая ошибка в мире!
② hard ≠ hardly. "She works hard" = молодец. "She hardly works" = лентяйка! Совсем разные значения.
③ fast, hard, early, late — одинаковы как прилагательное и наречие. "A fast car" (adj) / "She drives fast" (adv). Никакого -ly!

💡 Позиция: наречие образа действия стоит ПОСЛЕ глагола или ПОСЛЕ объекта — никогда между ними: ✅ "She reads carefully" / ✅ "She reads the text carefully" / ✗ "She reads carefully the text"

exercises.text: Amir plans his week very ___ — he writes every task in advance.
exercises.hint: careful (adj) → carefully (adverb). Describes HOW he plans: carefully.
good → well (irregular). "She speaks English well." NOT "goodly" or "good".

exercises.text: "She studies hardly every day" means she is a very hard-working student.
exercises.hint: "hardly" = almost not / barely. "She hardly studies" = she barely studies. The correct form: "She studies hard."

exercises.instruction: Which sentence has the correct word order?
exercises.hint: Adverb of manner goes AFTER the object: "explained the problem clearly" ✅

exercises.text: Zhibek ___  (easy) passes all her grammar tests.
exercises.hint: easy → easily. Adjective ending in -y: drop y, add -ily. (happy→happily, heavy→heavily)
"She is a GOOD student." (adjective modifies noun) / "She studies WELL." (adverb modifies verb).
"fastly" and "goodly" don't exist. "quicklier" is wrong. "hardly" exists but means "almost not" — different from "hard"!

exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct adverb.
exercises.text: The robot moves ___ — it changes direction without any human input. (automatic)
exercises.hint: automatic + ally = automatically. Adjectives ending in -ic form adverbs with -ally.
easy → easily. -y ending: drop y, add -ily. (heavy→heavily, happy→happily)

exercises.instruction: Correct the sentence — write the correct word.
exercises.hint: good (adjective) → well (adverb). Describes HOW she speaks. "She speaks well." ✅
Adverb of manner goes AFTER the object: "reads the notes carefully" ✅. Never between verb and object.

exercises.text: "She hardly studies" means she is a very hard-working student.
exercises.hint: "hardly" = almost not / barely. "She hardly studies" = she barely does any work. Correct form for effort: "She studies hard."

questions.hint: Most adjectives → add -ly: careful + ly = carefully.
good → well. The most important irregular adverb. "She speaks English well." (NOT "goodly"!)

questions.text: "She works ___." — She puts in a lot of effort.
questions.hint: hard (adverb) = with effort. "She works hard." hardly = almost not — very different!

questions.text: "She runs fastly every morning." is correct English.
questions.hint: "fastly" does not exist! fast stays as fast: "She runs fast." (same form for adjective and adverb)

questions.text: Which sentence has the CORRECT word order?
questions.hint: Adverb of manner goes AFTER the object: "explained the problem clearly" ✅
-y ending: drop y, add -ily → easy→easily. (heavy→heavily, lucky→luckily)
good = adjective (before noun). well = adverb (after verb). "a good student" / "studies well".

questions.text: "He hardly ever misses class." This means he:
questions.hint: "hardly ever" = almost never. It's a NEGATIVE meaning: "He almost never misses class." ✅

questions.text: "She quickly reads the textbook" is grammatically correct.
questions.hint: Adverbs can also go BEFORE the verb (especially in formal writing): "She quickly reads..." ✅ Both positions can be correct.

questions.text: He drives very ___ — he never exceeds the speed limit. (slow)
Which adverb is an IRREGULAR form (same as adjective)?
questions.hint: early stays as early (adjective and adverb). Also: fast, hard, late, high, low. These don't add -ly.
After an action verb (speaks), use adverb → well. "She speaks English well." The adverb form of good.

questions.text: "He studies ___ for exams — he barely opens a book."
questions.hint: "barely opens a book" = almost nothing → hardly. "hardly" = almost not. Negative meaning!
